name: Cartographer's Rest

stars.name: Rest
stars.notes: An old, stable orange dwarf whose slow, even burning has made it the traditional muster point for survey fleets heading into the Marches; its light is easy on instruments and on eyes.

planets.name: Inkstone
planets.notes: A dark basalt world mined once, briefly, for carbon before the Guild reserved the system; its black face still shows the scars of the first crude excavations.

planets.name: Marginalia
planets.notes: A wind-scoured desert where every returning survey crew paints its ship's name on a canyon wall; the markings now run for forty kilometers and are protected by charter.

planets.name: Atlas Minor
planets.notes: A thin-aired steppe world used for surface training; survey candidates spend a season here learning to map terrain the old way, on foot.

planets.name: Compass Rose
planets.notes: A calm amber giant whose magnetic field is stable enough to serve as the Marches' primary navigational bearing; every chart in the region is drawn relative to it.

planets.name: Last Light
planets.notes: The outermost marker of the settled Marches; beyond it the charts go blank by deliberate policy, and the blankness begins at its beacon.

asteroid_belts.name: The Drafting Board
asteroid_belts.notes: A broad belt used for shakedown cruises and instrument testing; its rocks are catalogued down to individual boulders, making it the best-surveyed debris field in the region.

stations.name: Cartographer's Rest Station
stations.notes: The Guild's forward base in the Marches: dry docks, chart libraries, crew housing, and the famous Map Room where every expedition briefs before crossing Last Light's beacon.

stations.name: Rose Anchorage
stations.notes: A civilian port serving the survey fleet; outfitters, repair yards, and the only permanent market for rimward data within thirty light-years.

faction_control.notes: The Guild administers the system as a professional commons: any licensed crew may berth, resupply, and buy chart access, provided they file their findings when they return. Most do. The ones who don't are remembered.

history: The station was founded during the Marches' first mapping era as a simple fuel cache and grew, expedition by expedition, into the region's institutional heart.

The tradition of painting ship names on Marginalia began with a lost crew who left their vessel's name so searchers would know they had made it this far; the searchers found the wreck, and kept the custom.

Twenty years ago the Guild sealed all charts beyond Last Light pending review after three expeditions vanished in the same uncharted volume; the seal holds, and the blank space on the maps has acquired a name nobody uses aloud.
description: An orange sun hangs over five quiet worlds arranged like tools on a workbench: a dark stone, a desert turned open-air archive, a training steppe, a great amber compass, and a frozen gatepost at the edge of the known. Nothing here is wild. Everything here is measured, twice if possible, and the measure is the point.

Cartographer's Rest runs on routine. Survey crews berth at Rose Anchorage, refit at the station's docks, argue methodology in the Map Room, and depart in loose convoys toward the sealed dark past Last Light. Twelve hundred Guild staff keep the machinery of exploration oiled, and the three thousand civilians of the Anchorage sell them rope, fuel, and rumors in equal measure.

But the maps have an edge now, and everyone at the Rest feels it. Three ships crossed the seal twenty years ago and none came back; the Guild will not say what the recovered flight recorders contained, or whether there were any. New crews still paint their names on Marginalia before departure. Lately, more of them have been adding a second line underneath: a date they intend to be back.
